penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: SFMC debugging requires expert-level diagnosis of each specific customer's configuration, AMPscript code, and platform state — this is inherently per-customer manual work that Claude cannot fully automate without significant human triage.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Customers hitting obscure platform bugs will expect interactive back-and-forth support to validate whether a suggested fix actually resolved their specific issue.

rationale: The buyer is real and named — marketing ops managers and email developers at enterprise SFMC accounts who are clearly in a paid, high-stakes context — and they do pay for adjacent tooling. However, the core problem (debugging specific, undocumented SFMC edge cases) is inherently per-incident and per-configuration: each debugging session requires understanding a unique setup, inspecting live data, and iterating on fixes, which demands human expert judgment that Claude cannot reliably automate end-to-end. The operational_autonomy score of 4 and the resulting -1.5 penalty for requires_human_fulfillment correctly sink the total to 3.3, well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: This idea would be a Claude-assisted SFMC debugging knowledge base or triage service — customers submit their SFMC bug symptoms and receive a structured diagnostic report and suggested fixes. The factory could build a simple intake form, a Claude prompt trained on SFMC documentation and known edge cases, and a Stripe link for per-incident ($150–$300) or monthly retainer ($500+) pricing. Sell via targeted outreach to SFMC Trailblazer Community members, LinkedIn marketing ops groups, and Stack Exchange SFMC regulars — all outreach requires operator approval before sending. However: delivery cannot be automated. Each SFMC issue is unique to the customer's org, data extensions, and live campaign state; Claude can provide general guidance but cannot actually inspect the customer's SFMC instance, run queries, or verify fixes. This means every ticket requires Youval or a hired expert to do real diagnostic work, making it a consulting business, not a software product. A solo non-technical operator cannot build and maintain a genuinely autonomous version of this — it would consume per-customer time indefinitely. Do not build.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy build gate (scored 4, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai build gate (scored 5, floor is 6). The core deliverable — resolving undocumented SFMC platform bugs for a specific customer configuration — cannot be automated by Claude without direct access to the customer's SFMC org. This is a consulting/agency service disguised as a product opportunity. Total of 3.3 is also below the validate threshold of 5.5, so drop is the correct stage.
